answers.observation: The screenshots alone cannot prove provenance, but the bound product receipts show zero target pose keys, zero actor pose keys after release, Blender/Bullet as the final-pose source and exact save/reopen deltas of 0.0 degrees.
The blue sphere, leading target and downstream row share a clear screen-space contact path; the tighter impact framing makes the initiating collision unambiguous.
The aftermath visibly differs from setup and preserves four separately readable resting bodies, grounded by their changed contact shadows.
The aftermath camera reframes the solver-dispersed bodies rather than holding the setup composition; bound framing records identify evaluated semantic world bounds as the source.
Frame 28 shows contact but almost no visible downstream angular response; it is a valid first-response receipt, not the strongest cinematic propagation moment.

The real solver result still reads as a polished toy demonstration: all four targets settle nearly exactly horizontal, and the stills lack motion blur, contact deformation, surface wear, secondary debris and other dynamic cues.

softwareLessons: Keep final transforms exclusively solver-owned; never repair an unattractive result by authoring target pose keys.
Choose the cinematic impact frame from evaluated motion, such as peak aggregate target angular velocity or mid-propagation target count, rather than equating first response with the best image.
Introduce deterministic, bounded initial-condition variation in spacing, yaw, friction and restitution so Bullet produces less uniformly flat aftermaths without sacrificing reproducibility.
Add allowlisted physical secondary-motion layers and shutter-aware motion blur; do not use dust, chips or camera shake to conceal weak primary collision behavior.
Separate causal correctness acceptance from filmic realism acceptance; this run closes the former only.
limitations: This proves one allowlisted declarative product workflow and one four-target fixture, not broad autonomous filmmaking.
The three stills demonstrate readable setup, contact and result but do not establish convincing continuous motion timing.
The visual style remains stylized and manufactured; photoreal material response, deformation, secondary motion and sound remain unproven.
